title: 3. Database tables and normalization
description: Modification anomalies (insertion, deletion, update), 1NF/2NF/3NF dependencies, candidate keys, and lossless decomposition.

items.question: A student's address is repeated across enrolments. Only one row is changed. What results?
items.explanation: Different rows now disagree about the same fact.

items.question: A subject cannot be added until a student enrols. What is this?
items.explanation: An independent fact cannot be added by itself.

items.question: Deleting the last enrolment erases the only record of the subject’s credit value. What is this?
items.explanation: Deleting one fact unintentionally removes another.

items.question: Several subject codes are stored in a single cell in a 0NF table. Which change addresses this for 1NF?

options.text: One row per student–subject pair, with a key

items.explanation: Separate the repeating values into individual rows.

items.title: Reference Scenario for Q20–23
items.content: ENROLMENT(SID, SubjectID, SName, SubjectDescription, Grade) contains atomic values. Its only candidate key is (SID, SubjectID). Assume SID → SName, SubjectID → SubjectDescription, and (SID, SubjectID) → Grade. Neither key component alone determines Grade.

items.question: What does SubjectID → SubjectDescription mean?
items.explanation: The dependency runs from ID to description, not necessarily the reverse.

items.question: Which is a full dependency on the composite key?
items.explanation: Grade requires the whole key; SName needs only SID.

items.question: What is ENROLMENT’s highest normal form?
items.explanation: Values are atomic, but partial dependencies prevent 2NF.

items.question: Which decomposition preserves the details and removes the partial dependencies?

options.text: STUDENT and SUBJECT with their own descriptions; ENROLMENT with both IDs and Grade
ENROLMENT with IDs and Grade only

items.explanation: Store facts with their determinants and preserve Grade at the pair level.

items.question: EMPLOYEE has only candidate key EmpID. EmpID → DeptID and DeptID → DeptName. What prevents 3NF?
items.explanation: EmpID determines DeptName indirectly via DeptID.

items.question: Which design fixes Q24 while retaining the department link?

options.text: EMPLOYEE(EmpID, EmpName, DeptID) and DEPARTMENT(DeptID, DeptName)
Remove DeptID from EMPLOYEE and keep DEPARTMENT separately
Keep the original and make DeptName unique

items.explanation: DeptID links to a single stored department name.
